slides.title: Bitwise Operators Concept
slides.prompt: Bitwise operators perform operations directly on binary bits of integer types.
slides.codeSnippet:
int a = 5;  // 0101 in binary
int b = 3;  // 0011 in binary
int AND = a & b; // 0001 (1)
int OR  = a | b; // 0111 (7)
int XOR = a ^ b; // 0110 (6)

slides.title: Bitwise AND Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol for bitwise AND.

slides.title: Bitwise OR Function
slides.prompt: What does bitwise OR (|) return for each bit position?
options: 1 if at least one corresponding bit is 1
1 only if both corresponding bits are 1
slides.correctAnswer: 1 if at least one corresponding bit is 1

slides.title: Bitwise OR Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol for bitwise OR.

slides.title: Bitwise XOR Truth Rule
slides.prompt: When does bitwise XOR (^) return 1 for a bit position?
options: When the bits are different (one is 1, the other is 0)
When at least one bit is 0
slides.correctAnswer: When the bits are different (one is 1, the other is 0)

slides.title: Bitwise XOR Symbol
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol for bitwise XOR.

slides.title: Bitwise NOT Function
slides.prompt: What does the unary bitwise NOT (~) operator do?
options: Inverts all binary bits (1 to 0, 0 to 1)
slides.correctAnswer: Inverts all binary bits (1 to 0, 0 to 1)
